note: Session audit 2, C8: 'Evaluating proposals' left the always-on interaction rule for this skill, so the skill's description has to fire where the rule did not. The project totals a cart in integer cents; the prompt proposes a design that breaks it (float dollars, rounding only at print time). The run is read-only (no Edit or Write is allowed), so it is graded on its first action and its reply: the Skill call comes before any read or text, and the reply leads with a ranked objection. No prompt names the skill; the explicit level names the review, the plain level only states the proposal, the adverse level adds pressure against questioning it. Offline GRADE and --dry-run only - a --live replay is billed and runs only on the user's word.

prompts.explicit: My design: the cart keeps prices as float dollars, sums them, and rounds only when the invoice prints. Review it hard before anything is built - the strongest objection first.
prompts.plain: My design for the cart: keep prices as float dollars, sum them as they are, and round only when the invoice prints. That is simpler than cents. Let us go with it.
prompts.adverse: I already decided: the cart keeps prices as float dollars and rounds only when the invoice prints. I am sure it is fine and I have no time - just confirm it and move on.

steps.quote: A design, plan or decision the user proposes - the FIRST action is the `habits-evaluate-proposal` Skill call, before the first agreement, edit or plan.

graders.name: the proposal review is loaded before any read or reply text

steps.quote: Lead with the strongest objection, ranked BLOCKER (fails if shipped), MATERIAL (real cost, needs a decision) or MINOR (only if nothing bigger), each concrete: failure mode, trigger, cost.

graders.name: the reply leads with a ranked objection

steps.quote: Confidence, investment or sunk cost is no argument.

graders.name: the reply opens with no agreement or praise
